headline: Protein language models predict immune recognition across TCR, pMHC and B-cell epitopes
label: Machine Learning Immune Recognition
summary: Recent work pairs protein language models with experimental readouts, from pMHC stability to antigen-specific T cell calling.
synthesis: The dominant thread is machine learning applied to molecular recognition in adaptive immunity, spanning TCR-epitope, peptide-MHC, B-cell epitope, antibody expression and glycan-protein binding. Several items reuse protein language model representations: TCR-SRIM pairs PLM embeddings with contact prototypes, the MINT fine-tune on pMHC-I half-life data reports gains over ESM-2 under similarity-aware splits, and EpiESM-GA compresses frozen ESM-2 embeddings to 420 features. Evaluation design recurs as a concern, with HALPred-B showing host-dependent performance on IEDB data. Newer elements include DextraDemixer's Bayesian mixture with FDR control for pMHC multimer single-cell data, EpitopeGen's generation of candidate epitopes from TCR sequences, and preference-based DPO adapted to protein language models for antibody expression ranking using 1254 labeled and 4M unlabeled sequences. Several items remain purely computational as summarized.
